card.name: Setting up whether something is desirable
card.fires_on: Words right before a judgment of whether something is good or bad, such as 'not such a bad thing' or 'can be a desirable event'. It appears in arguments that a feared thing (debt, fever, germs) is actually beneficial.

modes.label: Reframing a bad thing
modes.description: Words leading into 'bad thing' or 'desirable event' when the text argues something feared is actually fine or good.
modes.example: why that might not be such a<< bad>> thing.

modes.label: Treating as friend or sign
modes.description: Linking words where something feared (fever, germs) is treated as a positive sign or friend.
modes.example: some of us have begun to respect these germs<< as>> friends, not enemies.

modes.label: Acceptable effect in dosing
modes.description: A word before 'desirable' when a side effect such as drowsiness is called acceptable.
modes.example: drowsiness is not objectionable or is<< even>> desirable.

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward desirable, favorable or preferable.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to say that something is good, wanted or beneficial, often against expectation.
